text:
This was one of the craziest Laravel bugs I reported (CVE-2026-114508). A read-only GET request could wipe an entire database table 🚨  

With Laravel's JSON:API resources, changing ?include=comments to ?include=comments.truncate passed "truncate" straight to Eloquent without checking the child resource. Even though the request returned HTTP 500, Laravel had already run TRUNCATE TABLE comments.

Patched in Laravel 12.68.0 & 13.27.0 (PR #61322).  

More info 👇
